## Appearance

Isolde is an extremely lovely young woman with black hair, dark eyes, rosy cheeks marked with dimples, and a cheerful look. As a girl, she had a bright figure in her crimson ulster and wore dark ringlets. She has a rounder frame, self-consciously describing herself as a dumpling.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c25 P40](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0040), [v1 c33 P13](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0013), [v2 c27 P39](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0039), [v3 c2 P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004)_

## Personality

Isolde is cheerful, kind, good, and practical, serving as an exceptionally comforting companion. She is faithful and loyal, remaining steadfastly affectionate toward her friends and selflessly appreciative of their talents. Though lively and charming, she can be firm in her principles, such as refusing to speak to dishonest schoolmates or act as a snitch.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c15 P26](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0026), [v1 c19 P70](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0070), [v1 c21 P17](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0017), [v1 c37 P19](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0019), [v3 c12 P59](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0059)_

## History

Isolde grew up at Pear Hill and attended the school in Brierley under Mr. Pidgeon and later Miss Thorne. As a child, she established a deep friendship and solemn bond of comradeship with Nell Harcourt, with whom she created playhouses like Larkrise, invented fictional stories, and shared daily walks along the Aspen Path. Though briefly forbidden by her mother from speaking to Nell following a misunderstanding over currant wine, their friendship was quickly restored. During her school years, Isolde participated in the Story Club, sang encored solos at local concerts, and engaged in local social activities. Upon reaching adulthood, she joined the Brierley Village Improvement Society, serving as its treasurer. She became engaged to Gideon Duckett and married him a few years later, with Nell acting as her bridesmaid. Following her marriage, she gave birth to a son.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037), [v1 c12 P35](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0035), [v1 c13 P13](../source/v01-c13.md#nw-v01-c13-p0013), [v1 c15 P3](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0003), [v1 c16 P42](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0042), [v1 c18 P43](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0043), [v1 c25 P50](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0050), [v2 c6 P8](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0008), [v2 c29 P15](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0015), [v3 c11 P43](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0043), [v3 c28 P23](../source/v03-c28.md#nw-v03-c28-p0023), [v3 c39 P41](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0041)_

## Background by volume

- received her name because a schoolmaster lodged at her home when she was born  <sub>[v1 c2 P64](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0064)</sub>
- visited her aunt in Delford  <sub>[v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037)</sub>
- learned a decorative crochet stitch from her aunt in Delford  <sub>[v1 c18 P49](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0049)</sub>
- belonged to a school Story Club as a girl  <sub>[v3 c11 P43](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0043), [v3 c12 P10](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0010)</sub>
- recollected being struck by her mother as a child  <sub>[v3 c39 P47](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0047)</sub>
- confined to her house due to a severe bout of bronchitis  <sub>[v3 c18 P3](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0003)</sub>

## Quotes

> Every one of those Tulk girls acts dishonestly. Yesterday, Tibby Tulk literally set her milk bottle where mine belonged in the brook. Can you imagine? Now I refuse to talk to her.  <sub>[v1 c15 P26](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0026)</sub>

> Is it probable that I would act in that way? Nell Harcourt, I am not a snitch, and besides, the fault was equally mine.  <sub>[v1 c19 P70](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0070)</sub>

> I would desire to be slender and tall.  <sub>[v2 c13 P33](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0033)</sub>

> I am so eager for the time when he is big enough to speak. Hearing him call me ‘mother’ is my deepest desire. And oh, I am resolved that he will have a pleasant first recollection of me. My own earliest remembrance of my mother involves her striking me because of an act I had committed. I have no doubt that I merited the punishment, and my mother was invariably wonderful and holds a special place in my heart. Even so, I truly wish that my initial memory concerning her had been more agreeable.  <sub>[v3 c39 P47](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0047)</sub>
